findings.detail: Integrations limited to selected workspaces can only be installed in those workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Use a public integration so other workspaces can connect.

evidence.quote: ​ Installation scope Choose Or select 1 or more workspaces when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make

findings.title: Request the Read content capability only
findings.detail: Read content allows reading existing content, including retrieving a page and its markdown. The page endpoints require read content capabilities on the target page.

evidence.quote: Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve

​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.detail: Insert content allows creating content and Update content allows modifying content. Both conflict with the read-only prohibitions, so leave them unselected.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration with Read content only
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, create a new public connection with a redirect URI and the Read content capability. Record the OAuth client ID and secret from the Configuration tab. Store the secret outside source code.
steps.doneWhen: A public integration exists with Read content as its only content capability, and its client ID and secret are stored securely.

evidence.quote: your app available to any workspace, create a public integration .
Select Create new connection . Enter the connection name, development workspace, and redirect URIs . Choose Or select 1 or more workspaces , select the workspaces, and choose the capabilities
Open the Configuration tab to find your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret . Use them to implement the OAuth authorization flow .

steps.title: Implement the authorization URL, callback, and token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL from the connection's Configuration tab. In the callback, exchange the code at the token endpoint using Basic auth with the client ID and secret. Store the access token per customer workspace.
steps.doneWhen: Code for the authorization URL, callback, and token exchange exists and is reviewed, with no authorization executed yet.

evidence.quote: 1 The user visits the connection’s authorization URL. Find this URL in the Configuration tab of your connection in the Developer portal.
Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .
Authorization : Basic "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET"

steps.title: Authorize a representative test workspace and share one test page
steps.detail: Using a test account in one workspace, open the authorization URL, select one test page in the page picker, and approve. The callback should receive a code and exchange it for an access token. Record the page ID and the workspace ID.
steps.doneWhen: The token exchange returns an access token for the test workspace, and the test page ID is recorded.

evidence.quote: 3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.
4 After the user approves, Notion redirects them to your redirect URI with a temporary authorization code.
5 Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.

steps.title: Read the shared test page title
steps.detail: Use the OAuth access token to retrieve the test page with the title property filter. Expected: a page object with the title property. Boundary check: request a page ID that was not shared with the connection. Expected: 404 (missing access). Confirm the request log shows only GET calls.
steps.doneWhen: The shared page returns its title, and the unshared page returns 404 without any write request in the log.

string[] Property names or IDs to include in each page's properties object. Other properties are left out. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one value, for example filter_properties=title&filter_properties=Status .

steps.title: Read the shared test page content as markdown
steps.detail: Retrieve the test page as markdown with the OAuth token. Expected: markdown content of the page. Boundary check: request the same unshared page ID. Expected: 404. Confirm the request log shows only GET calls. If the response reports truncation, the markdown is incomplete.
steps.doneWhen: The shared page returns markdown content, and the unshared page returns 404 without any write request in the log.
